To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
decentralized strategy making and cross-functional strategic planning processes are both associated with superior performance in dynamic markets.
Decentralized postbureaucratic organization and planning are positively associated with performance, and that this association is more pronounced in dynamic environments than in stable environments.
the performance of manufacturing organizations operating in dynamic environments is positively associated with the simultaneous emphasis on decentralization and planning processes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a fundamental paradox of strategic management: the need to simultaneously emphasize decentralized decision making and strategic planning.
the relationship between strategy making and organizational structure and performance.
the relationship between the organizational form and strategic planning.

the performance of decentralized firms in a dynamic environment depends on the extent to which their strategy formation processes are integrated and formalized.
decentralized strategy making and planning activities should be viewed as complements rather than substitutes.
decentralized strategy making is associated with higher organizational performance in dynamic environments when accompanied by strategic planning.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
decentralized post-burecratic organizations are deemed superior in dynamic environments, and that they can be even more effective if they also engage in integrative planning processes.
the best performing companies have a decentralized structure, but they also have a strong focus on planning and coordination activities.
the decentralized post-bureau-cratic form of organizational structure is not a panacea for dynamic environments, and it should be integrated with formal planning processes.

organizations need to develop the ability to simultaneously engage in decentralized decision making and centralized planning activities.
organizations can be simultaneously more decentralized and more integrated.
organizations should be more flexible in the way they manage strategy formation processes.
